subject: Extract log likelihood for hBayesDM models

messages.author: 6403ad2aa9ae6d03
messages.subject: Extract log likelihood for hBayesDM models
parts:
Hi,

I'm interested in comparing an hBayesDM model (specifically, a model produced by the bandit2arm_delta() function) to another model computed using functions from Python. I plan to do so by computing the BIC for each model using the useBICCustom() function from the AICcmodavg package. 

On pg. 41 of Ahn, Haines, & Zhang (2017), the authors indicate that the log likelihood is computed for each participant using the following bit of code:

model {

      …

       for (i in 1:N) {

        for (t in 1:T) {

         Choice[i, t] ∼ categorical_logit(ev);

      …

      }

      Generated quantities {

      …

       for (i in 1:N) {

        log_lik[i] = 0;

        for (t in 1:T) {

         log_lik[i]=log_lik[i] + categorical_logit_lpmf(Choice[i, t] | ev);

      …

      }

So, it seems like I should be able to extract the log_lik value indexed for each participant, and then compute the BIC values from there.

My question, then, is: How can I extract the log_lik value from the bandit2arm_delta() function? 

Best,

Thomas McCauley
Ph.D. student
Department of Psychology
University of California, San Diego

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Extract log likelihood for hBayesDM models
parts:
Hi Thomas, 

Sorry for the long delay!

Here's a sample code. 

output = bandit2arm_delta("example", 2000, 1000, 2, 2)

--> You can extract "log_lik" with 

output$parVals$log_lik

Best,
Young
